academic_translation:
If even a misdeed committed in a single instant
Leads to dwelling in the Avīci hell for an eon,
Due to the misdeeds accumulated in beginningless saṃsāra,
What need is there to mention that one will not go to a happy realm?
translation: Just one instant of a harmful deed can trap me in Avichi for a great age. I have gathered harmful deeds in the cycle of rebirth, which has no beginning. So of course I will not go to a happy realm!

academic_translation:
Having experienced just that much,
One will not attain liberation,
Because while experiencing it in this way,
Other misdeeds are fully generated.
translation: I will not win freedom just by living through that. While I am experiencing it, I will just create other harmful deeds.

academic_translation:
Having found such leisure as this,
If I do not habituate myself to virtue,
There is no other deception than this,
And there is no other bewilderment than this.
translation: I have found this freedom to practice. If I do not build a habit of doing good deeds, there is no worse trick than this. There is no worse confusion than this.

academic_translation:
If, having understood this,
I am still lazy later out of bewilderment,
At the time of death,
Great sorrow will arise.
translation: If I understand this but stay lazy because I am confused, great sorrow will come to me when it is time to die.

academic_translation:
If the unbearable fire of hell
Burns my body for a long time,
Due to the blazing fire of unbearable regret,
My mind will doubtless be tormented.
translation: If the unbearable fire of hell burns my body for a long time, my mind will surely be tormented by the blazing fire of unbearable regret.

academic_translation:
This state of benefit that is extremely difficult to find,
Having found it by some chance,
If, while I myself possess understanding,
I am led back again to that hell,
translation: This helpful state is very hard to find. Somehow, I have found it by chance. But what if, even while I understand this, I am led back again to that hell?

academic_translation:
As if bewildered by a mantra,
I am reduced to having no mind here.
Even I do not know what bewilders me;
What is there inside me?
translation: It is as if I have been confused by sacred words. I am left with no mind here. I do not even know what is confusing me. What is inside me?

academic_translation:
The enemies, hatred, craving, and so forth,
Have no hands, feet, and so forth,
And are neither brave nor wise; yet how is it
That they have made me like a slave?
translation: My enemies, like hatred and wanting, do not have hands or feet. They are not brave or wise. So how have they made me like a slave?

academic_translation:
While dwelling within my mind,
they do harm to me at their pleasure;
to not be angry even at that and to practice patience
is misplaced patience, an object of reproach.
translation: These enemies live right inside my mind. They hurt me whenever they want. If I do not get angry at them and just practice patience, that is the wrong kind of patience. I should be scolded for it.

academic_translation:
Even if the gods and asuras
all rose up against me as enemies,
even they would be unable to lead
and cast me into the fire of the Avīci hell.
translation: Even if all the gods and demigods rose up against me as enemies, they could not drag me away. They could not throw me into the fire of the Avichi hell.

academic_translation:
This powerful enemy, the afflictions,
casts me in a single instant there
where, upon contact, even Mount Meru
does not remain even as ashes.
translation: But my powerful enemy, these troubling emotions, can throw me there in a single instant. If Mount Meru touched that fire, it would burn away without leaving even ashes.

academic_translation:
These enemies of mine, the afflictions,
are long-lasting, as if without beginning or end;
all other enemies are incapable
of lasting for such a long time.
translation: My troubling emotions are enemies that last a very long time. They seem to have no beginning and no end. All my other enemies could never last that long.

academic_translation:
If amiably served and honored,
all others bring benefit and happiness;
but if the afflictions are served,
they bring further suffering and harm.
translation: If I serve and honor my other enemies, they might bring me help and happiness. But if I serve my troubling emotions, they only bring me more suffering and harm.

academic_translation:
Thus, if these long-standing, continuous enemies,
the sole cause for the great increase of a multitude of harms,
truly take up residence within my heart,
how could I be fearless and joyful in saṃsāra?
translation: These enemies have stayed with me for a long time without stopping. They are the only reason I suffer so many harms. If they truly live inside my heart, how could I be fearless and happy in the cycle of rebirth?

academic_translation:
If these guards of the prison of saṃsāra,
Who become executioners in hell and so forth,
Remain within the net of attachment dwelling in the mind,
How could there be happiness for me?
translation: These inner enemies guard the prison of the cycle of rebirth. They become executioners in hell. If they stay inside my mind in a net of clinging, how could I ever be happy?

academic_translation:
Thus, as long as I do not manifestly
And certainly destroy this enemy, I shall not forsake my effort here.
For instance, angered even by a slight wrongdoer,
Those swollen with pride do not sleep until they have destroyed that enemy.
translation: So, until I completely destroy this enemy, I will not give up my effort. Think of people who are filled with pride. If someone wrongs them just a little, they get angry. They do not sleep until they have destroyed that enemy.

academic_translation:
Those wretched enemies made to suffer by natural death—
If even those who desire to forcefully destroy them when arrayed in battle,
Having disregarded the suffering of being struck by arrows, spears, and weapons,
Do not turn back and flee without accomplishing their goal,
translation: In battle, soldiers fight enemies who will die a natural death anyway. These soldiers ignore the suffering of being struck by arrows, spears, and weapons. They do not turn back and run away without reaching their goal.

academic_translation:
The constant cause of all suffering—
Today, as I strive to destroy these definite natural enemies,
Whatever becomes the cause of hundreds of sufferings,
Needless to say, will not make me despair and lose heart.
translation: My true natural enemies are the constant cause of all suffering. Today, I am trying hard to destroy them. Even if this fight causes me hundreds of sufferings, it will certainly not make me despair and lose heart.

academic_translation:
If even the scars that enemies inflict for no meaningful purpose
Are worn like ornaments upon the body,
For me, who perfectly strives to accomplish the great purpose,
Why should suffering be a harm?
translation: People sometimes wear scars from meaningless fights with enemies like decorations on their bodies. I am working hard to achieve a truly great goal. Why should suffering be a harm to me?

academic_translation:
If fishermen, outcastes, farmers, and so forth,
Thinking only of their own mere livelihood,
Endure the harms of cold, heat, and so forth,
Why should someone like me not endure them for the happiness of wandering beings?
translation: Fishermen, outcasts, farmers, and others only think about making a living. Yet they put up with the pain of cold and heat. I am working for the happiness of all wandering beings. Why should someone like me not endure these things too?

academic_translation:
To liberate from afflictions the wandering beings
Who reach to the ends of space in the ten directions,
When I promised this, I myself
Was not freed from afflictions.
translation: I promised to free the wandering beings who fill space in the ten directions. I promised to free them from their troubling emotions. But when I made this promise, I was not even free from my own troubling emotions!

academic_translation:
Without even knowing my own measure,
How am I not a madman to speak thus?
Therefore, in destroying afflictions,
I shall never turn back.
translation: Since I do not even know what I can really do, am I not crazy to talk like this? Still, I will never turn back from destroying my troubling emotions.

academic_translation:
I shall be attached to this,
And, holding a grudge, engage in battle;
Afflictions of such a kind
Are excepted from what is to be abandoned, since they destroy afflictions.
translation: I will hold tightly to this goal. I will hold a grudge and fight this battle! This is the only kind of troubling emotion I should not let go of, because it destroys all other troubling emotions.

academic_translation:
Even if I am burned and killed,
Or even if my head is severed, so be it;
I shall never, in any circumstance,
Bow down to the enemies, the afflictions.
translation: Even if I am burned and killed, so be it. Even if my head is cut off, that is fine. But I will never bow down to my enemies, the troubling emotions.

academic_translation:
Even when ordinary enemies are expelled from a country,
They reside in other lands and take possession,
And having gathered strength, return from there;
But the way of the enemies, the afflictions, is not like that.
translation: When normal enemies are chased out of a country, they go live in other lands. They build up their strength and come back. But my enemies, the troubling emotions, are not like that.

academic_translation:
Afflictions, wretched afflictions, are to be abandoned by the eye of wisdom;
Expelled from my mind, where will they go?
Where will they dwell, to return and harm me?
It is only that I, being weak-minded, lack effort.
translation: These awful troubling emotions can be cleared away by the eye of wisdom. Once they are chased out of my mind, where will they go? Where could they hide to come back and hurt me? The truth is just that my mind is weak and I am not trying hard enough.

academic_translation:
Afflictions do not reside in sense objects, nor in the collection of faculties, nor in between.
If not elsewhere either, where do they reside and harm all wandering beings?
They are like an illusion; therefore, abandon fear in the heart and rely on effort in order to know them.
Why do I pointlessly harm myself in hells and so forth?
translation: Troubling emotions do not live in the things we sense. They do not live in the group of senses, or in between. If they are nowhere else, where do they stay to harm all beings? They are like an illusion. So, let go of fear in your heart and work hard to know them. Why do I hurt myself for no reason in the hells and other places?

academic_translation:
Having reflected in this way, I shall make effort
To accomplish the training just as it has been explained.
If one does not listen to the physician's words,
How can a patient who needs to be treated by medicines be cured?
translation: Thinking like this, I will work hard. I will do the training just as it was taught. If a sick person does not listen to the doctor, how can medicine cure them?

academic_translation: The fourth chapter from Entering the Way of the Bodhisattva, called Heedfulness.

locked_terms.use: Entering the Way of the Awakening Hero

translation: The fourth chapter from Entering the Way of the Awakening Hero, called Carefulness.

academic_translation:
Those who wish to guard the training
Must strictly guard the mind;
If this mind is not guarded,
One will be completely unable to guard the training.
translation: If you want to guard the training, you must guard your mind well. If this mind is not guarded, you cannot guard the training at all.

academic_translation:
Letting the elephant of the mind run loose
Inflicts harm in the Avīci hell;
An untamed, maddened elephant
Does not inflict such harm here.
translation: Letting the elephant of the mind run wild causes harm in the Avichi hell. A wild, crazy elephant here does not cause that much harm.

academic_translation:
If, with the rope of mindfulness on all sides,
The elephant of the mind is firmly bound,
All fears will cease to be,
And all virtues will come into one's hands.
translation: If I tightly tie up the elephant of the mind with the rope of keeping in mind, all fears will disappear. Every good deed will come right into my hands.

academic_translation:
Tigers, lions, elephants, bears,
Snakes, and all enemies,
Hell guardians, and
Witches, and likewise rākṣasas—
translation: There are tigers, lions, elephants, bears, snakes, and all enemies. There are hell guardians, witches, and also demons.

academic_translation:
By binding this mind alone,
All of them will be bound;
By subduing this mind alone,
All of them will be subdued.
translation: If I tie up this mind alone, all of those things are tied up. If I tame this mind alone, all of them are tamed.

academic_translation:
Thus, all fears and
Immeasurable sufferings too
Arise from the mind,
As the Speaker of Truth Himself has taught.
translation: All fears and endless suffering come from the mind. This is what the Speaker of Truth himself has taught.

academic_translation:
The weapons of the hell of sentient beings,
Who intentionally created them?
Who created the burning iron ground?
From what did those groups of women arise?
translation: Who purposely made the weapons in the hell of living beings? Who created the burning iron ground? Where did those groups of women come from?

academic_translation:
All such things as these
Were taught by the Sage to arise from the mind of misdeed.
Thus, in the three worlds,
There is no fear other than the mind.
translation: The Sage taught that all these things come from a harmful mind. So, in the three worlds, there is no other fear besides the mind.

academic_translation:
If removing the poverty of wandering beings
Is the perfection of generosity,
Since destitute wandering beings still exist,
How did the past Saviours reach perfection?
translation: If the perfection of giving means taking away the poverty of all beings, how did the past Protectors reach perfection? There are still poor beings today.

academic_translation:
All possessions together with their results,
Through the mind of relinquishing them to all people,
The perfection of generosity is taught;
Therefore, it is the mind itself.
translation: The perfection of giving is taught as having the mind of giving everything away. It means wanting to give all your things and their good results to everyone. Therefore, it is just the mind itself.

academic_translation:
Where could fish and so forth
Be banished so that they are not killed?
From attaining the mind of renunciation,
The perfection of ethical discipline is explained.
translation: Where could fish and other animals be put so they are never killed? The perfection of good conduct comes from getting the mind of giving up harmful actions.
